text: On a damp Thursday morning in late October, field staff at the Wyrmwood reserve opened two transport crates and watched three pine martens slip into the heather and spruce, the first reintroduction of the species there in more than a century. The move follows six years of planning by reserve ecologists and the Northfold Heritage Trust, which restored den sites, tightened road monitoring and reduced illegal trapping across the 4,800-acre woodland. Historian Edda Moor said old estate ledgers last recorded pine martens in Wyrmwood in 1909, before habitat loss and persecution drove them out. For now, the animals are fitted with radio tags, and wardens expect them to range widely through the winter as the reserve begins to recover a missing thread in its ecology.
